hook.title: Bring your React app. Keep shipping while you move.
hook.lede: Point `react` at `@pyreon/react-compat` and your hooks, deps arrays and all, run on Pyreon's engine. Then convert one component at a time, with a codemod for the mechanical parts, until the compat layer has nothing left to do.

steps.title: Install the compat layer
steps.text: The React layer plus the Pyreon runtime it sits on. The Vite plugin needs Vite 8. On the published packages `vite dev` renders a blank page (the compat JSX runtime ships no `jsxDEV`); `vite build` works, and the fix is on main for the next release.

steps.title: Change two config files
steps.text: Swap `@vitejs/plugin-react` for the Pyreon plugin in compat mode. It resolves `react`, `react-dom`, `react-dom/client` and the JSX runtime to the compat package, so your import lines stay as they are, and it renames `className` and `htmlFor` on the way through.

steps.title: Keep shipping
steps.text: Function components behave like React: `useState` returns the value, the body re-runs, deps arrays are honoured. Before you deploy, check the four known gaps: class components are stubs, transitions run synchronously, a child's state resets when its parent re-renders (lift that state up), and libraries that reach into React internals will not run.

steps.title: Convert one component at a time
steps.text: Run the codemod on a file, finish what it reports, and wrap the converted component in `nativeCompat()` so it runs in Pyreon's setup frame. The compat build skips Pyreon's compiler pass, so write reactive text as an arrow (`{() => …}`) until step 5.

steps.title: Switch the compiler on
steps.text: When no React-style component is left, drop `compat` from the plugin and set `jsxImportSource` to `@pyreon/core`. The compiler now makes `{likes()}` reactive without the arrow, and the app is plain Pyreon. Moving to Zero's file router is a separate step you can take later.

items.name: `migrate_react`
items.what: Your AI assistant hands it a React file and gets back `useState` turned into `signal`, `useMemo` into `computed`, `useEffect` into `effect`, `useCallback` unwrapped to a plain function, `className` and `htmlFor` renamed, `onChange` on inputs turned into `onInput`, the imports swapped, plus the list of changes it made and the findings it could not fix.
items.limits: A first pass that does not run as is: setter calls such as `setCount(…)` stay dangling, value reads are not turned into calls, a `useRef` becomes a signal so its `.current` uses break, and a `memo()` wrapper can stay in place although the change list says it was removed. `.map()` lists are flagged for `<For>` but not rewritten; class components and React-specific libraries are not converted. TypeScript flags the dangling setters; review the diff.

items.name: `pyreon check --fix`
items.what: The same detectors in the terminal. It scans your git-changed files (or the paths you pass), prints each finding with its fix, writes the codemod's first-pass rewrites with `--fix`, and exits non-zero on any finding, so it works as a pre-commit gate.
items.limits: Applies the same codemod as `migrate_react`, with the same gaps, and skips a file whose only React habit is a `.map()` list, an `onChange` or `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

items.name: `--compat` scaffold
items.what: Starting a new app next to the old one? The scaffold wires the compat layer into a Zero app for React, Vue, Solid or Preact.
items.limits: The scaffold offers `react`, `vue`, `solid` and `preact`; Svelte compat is set up by hand through the Vite plugin.

guidesTitle: No compat layer, still a guide.

cta.title: Ship on Pyreon this week. Finish the move when it pays.
